bull.b: Rapid bookings growth, a sharply expanded pipeline, and $38.3 million of remaining performance obligations indicate rising commercial demand. With most RPO expected within 24 months, this backlog provides measurable visibility into future revenue conversion and supports continued customer expansion.

A broad customer base and growing commercial-enterprise contribution suggest D-Wave is moving beyond research use toward repeatable business adoption. Production deployments with major organizations can create reference accounts, strengthen credibility, and support more durable sales across industries.

Very low leverage gives D-Wave greater flexibility to fund research, product development, and commercialization without substantial debt-service pressure. The sizable equity base also provides a buffer while the company works to convert technological progress and demand into sustainable operating returns.

bear.b: The company remains far from self-funding, consuming substantial cash to support operations and investment. Continued negative operating and free cash flow can reduce financial flexibility over time and increase the importance of successful revenue scaling, cost discipline, or additional capital.

Higher operating expenses combined with declining gross margin make it harder for revenue growth to translate into improved profitability. The pressure is especially relevant as professional services represented a larger mix, while accelerated product and go-to-market spending keeps the cost base elevated.

The potential CHIPS Act support is not yet available as operating or development cash because it remains subject to specified milestones. Until funding is received, D-Wave must continue financing its ambitious hardware roadmap against a backdrop of heavy cash consumption and large operating losses.
